--- .opencode/plans/ci-green-pr7-pr8.md

@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+# Plan: Make PR #7 and PR #8 CI green
+
+Both PRs in alehar9320/agentic-odi have failing CI. Fix root causes with real
+fixes (tests first), verify locally mirroring CI, push, watch checks.
+
+Global constraints:
+- Never weaken security scanning to get green (no bandit config skips).
+- Mirror CI commands exactly for local verification.
+- Work only in the two existing worktrees:
+  - PR #8: .worktrees/cli-bundled-distribution (feature/cli-bundled-distribution)
+  - PR #7: .worktrees/living-studio-tauri (topic/living-studio-tauri)
+- No rebase needed (both MERGEABLE on current origin/main).
+
+## Root causes (evidence verified)
+
+### PR #8 — security job (then CI green; smoke skipped, never ran)
+Bandit, 6 issues in cli/src:
+1. B110 (low) cli/src/cli/cli.py:42-43 — `except Exception: pass` in `_startup_auto_update`
+2. B606 (low) cli/src/cli/cli.py:78 — `os.execv` re-exec of own binary
+3. B202 (med) cli/src/cli/update.py:79 — `zf.extractall(dest)` (bandit flags any
+   `extractall` when the module also imports `tarfile`; CPython `_extract_member`
+   strips `..`/absolute paths — verified in stdlib source)
+4. B202 (med) cli/src/cli/update.py:82 — `tf.extractall(dest)` unvalidated
+5. B310 (high) cli/src/cli/update.py:168 — `urlopen` (`# noqa: S310` affects neither ruff nor bandit)
+6. B310 (high) cli/src/cli/update.py:173 — same
+All other scanned srcs clean. Bandit accepts literal `filter="data"` kwarg
+(verified in bandit 1.9.4 plugin source: returns None → no issue).
+All URLs derive from https constants (RELEASES_API, _RELEASES_DOWNLOAD).
+
+### PR #7 — studio + tauri-build + smoke (then CI green)
+1. TS2307 `Cannot find module '../../lib/odi'` — `studio/src/lib/{odi.ts,odi.test.ts}`
+   exist on disk but were never committed: root `.gitignore` unanchored `lib/`
+   (stock Python template) swallows any dir named lib. Verified: root `lib/` never
+   existed in history, no script writes it, all Python pkgs use src/ layout,
+   venv libs covered by `.venv/`/`venv/`/`env/`.
+2. Smoke sidecar probe 422s: POST `/api/health/mcp` with `{}` but
+   `McpHealthRequest.mcp_url` is required; GET `/api/canvas` missing required
+   `mcp_url` query. Both curl legs fail (verified in run log + router.py + tests).
+3. Steps never reached after early failures: studio unit tests/build/gen-check,
+   client.run smoke step — must de-risk locally.
+Decision (user-approved evaluation): anchor `lib/` → `/lib/`, `lib64/` → `/lib64/`;
+keep the canonical `studio/src/lib` name (industry-standard TS source dir).
+
+## Task 1: PR #8 — failing tests first
+- Worktree cli-bundled-distribution. In cli/tests/test_update.py add:
+  - `test_extract_archive_rejects_tar_path_traversal`: tar with member
+    `../escape.txt` → `extract_archive` must raise and no file may appear outside dest.
+    RED now (extractall without filter writes outside).
+  - `test_extract_archive_contains_zip_path_traversal`: zip member `../evil.txt`
+    → extracted only under dest, no escape (documents zipfile sanitization).
+  - `test_default_fetch_rejects_non_https`: `update._default_fetch("file:///<tmp>")`
+    → raises `update.UpdateError` and does not return file content. RED now.
+Expected: pytest shows the two RED tests failing for the right reasons.
+
+## Task 2: PR #8 — real fixes
+- update.py `extract_archive`: tar branch → `tf.extractall(dest, filter="data")`;
+  zip branch → keep + `# nosec B202 - ZipFile._extract_member strips absolute/'..' paths`.
+- update.py: add `_require_https(url)` (raise `UpdateError` unless scheme == "https"),
+  call from `_default_fetch` and `_default_fetch_bytes`; replace `# noqa: S310` with
+  `# nosec B310 - scheme enforced by _require_https`.
+- cli.py: `pass` → `return None` (keep `# noqa: BLE001`).
+- cli.py:78: trailing `# nosec B606` + justification (re-execs own verified binary).
+Expected: new tests GREEN; full cli suite GREEN.
+
+## Task 3: PR #8 — local CI mirror + smoke de-risk
+- `uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src connectors/src` → exit 0
+- `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` → clean
+- mypy: `uv run --directory <pkg> mypy .` for core, mcp_server, local_server, cli, client, connectors
+- `uv run --directory cli pytest` → all pass
+- Smoke steps (never ran on this PR): `uv run python -m cli --version`;
+  `uv run python -m cli connectors --help` greps for list+ingest;
+  MCP server boot probe on :8000 (verbatim from ci.yml); client.run probe (verbatim).
+
+## Task 4: PR #8 — commit + push + watch
+- Commit with repo-style message; push; `gh pr checks 8 --watch`.
+
+## Task 5: PR #7 — gitignore + track src/lib
+- Worktree living-studio-tauri. Root `.gitignore`: `lib/` → `/lib/`, `lib64/` → `/lib64/`.
+- `git add studio/src/lib` (odi.ts, odi.test.ts); confirm nothing else newly unignored
+  (`git status --short` shows only intended files).
+
+## Task 6: PR #7 — fix smoke probe 422s
+- ci.yml sidecar probe:
+  - `-d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}'`
+  - `http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp`
+- Expected: both legs 200 (health returns reachable=false when MCP down; canvas
+  falls back to seed payload — verified in probes.py/mcp_data.py).
+
+## Task 7: PR #7 — local verification (incl. never-reached steps)
+- `cd studio && npm ci && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test -- --run
+  && npm run build && npm run gen:api-types && git diff --exit-code -- src/api/schema.d.ts`
+- Run edited sidecar probe verbatim (sidecar via `uv run python -m local_server.main`).
+- Run client.run probe verbatim (never ran in CI).
+- tauri-build: frontend `npm run build` is the actual CI failure (covered above);
+  cargo side previously green in tauri-check; full `npm run tauri build` only if
+  system webkit deps available locally.
+
+## Task 8: PR #7 — commit + push + watch
+- Commit; push; `gh pr checks 7 --watch`.
+
+## Task 9: Final review
+- Review both diffs against plan; verification-before-completion before any
+  success claim; report rulings/deferreds.

+"""Tests for the CLI backend abstraction."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import re
+
+from cli.backend import BackendConfig, LocalBackend, MCPBackend, resolve_backend
+
+
+def _id_from(text: str) -> str:
+    match = re.search(r"({.*})", text)
+    assert match is not None, text
+    return json.loads(match.group(1))["id"]  # type: ignore[index]
+
+
+def test_local_backend_full_crud_round_trip(tmp_path):
+    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
+    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=db)
+    job_text = backend.call("add_job", {"name": "J", "description": "d"})
+    assert "created successfully" in job_text
+    import json
+    import re
+
+    job_id = json.loads(re.search(r"({.*})", job_text).group(1))["id"]  # type: ignore[union-attr]
+    backend.call("add_step", {"job_id": job_id, "name": "S", "order": 1})
+    backend.call(
+        "add_outcome",
+        {
+            "job_id": job_id,
+            "statement": "Min x",
+            "importance": 8.0,
+            "satisfaction": 4.0,
+        },
+    )
+    listed = backend.call("get_outcomes", {"job_id": job_id})
+    assert "Min x" in listed
+    assert json.loads(backend.call("get_jobs", {}))[0]["name"] == "J"
+
+
+def test_resolve_backend_warns_on_db_with_mcp(capsys):
+    resolve_backend(BackendConfig(backend="mcp", db_path="x.db", mcp_url="http://x/mcp"))
+    assert "ignored" in capsys.readouterr().err.lower()
+
+
+def test_resolve_backend_unknown_raises():
+    import pytest
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        resolve_backend(BackendConfig(backend="nope", db_path=None, mcp_url=None))
+
+
+def test_resolve_backend_returns_matching_backend_types(tmp_path):
+    local = resolve_backend(
+        BackendConfig(backend="local", db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"), mcp_url=None)
+    )
+    assert isinstance(local, LocalBackend)
+    mcp = resolve_backend(BackendConfig(backend="mcp", db_path=None, mcp_url="http://x/mcp"))
+    assert isinstance(mcp, MCPBackend)
+
+
+def test_local_backend_job_step_outcome_lifecycle(tmp_path):
+    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))
+    job_id = _id_from(backend.call("add_job", {"name": "J"}))
+
+    assert json.loads(backend.call("get_job", {"job_id": job_id}))["name"] == "J"
+    assert "Job updated successfully" in backend.call(
+        "update_job", {"job_id": job_id, "name": "J2"}
+    )
+    assert json.loads(backend.call("get_job", {"job_id": job_id}))["name"] == "J2"
+
+    step_id = _id_from(backend.call("add_step", {"job_id": job_id, "name": "S", "order": 1}))
+    job_map = backend.call("get_job_map", {"job_id": job_id})
+    assert json.loads(job_map)[0]["name"] == "S"
+    assert "Step updated successfully" in backend.call(
+        "update_step", {"step_id": step_id, "name": "S2"}
+    )
+    assert json.loads(backend.call("get_step", {"step_id": step_id}))["name"] == "S2"
+
+    outcome_id = _id_from(
+        backend.call(
+            "add_outcome",
+            {"job_id": job_id, "statement": "Min x", "importance": 8.0, "satisfaction": 4.0},
+        )
+    )
+    assert "Outcome updated successfully" in backend.call(
+        "update_outcome", {"outcome_id": outcome_id, "importance": 9.0}
+    )
+    assert json.loads(backend.call("get_outcome", {"outcome_id": outcome_id}))["importance"] == 9.0
+
+    assert "Step deleted successfully" in backend.call("delete_step", {"step_id": step_id})
+    assert "Outcome deleted successfully" in backend.call(
+        "delete_outcome", {"outcome_id": outcome_id}
+    )
+    assert "Job deleted successfully" in backend.call("delete_job", {"job_id": job_id})
+
+
+def test_local_backend_not_found_messages(tmp_path):
+    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))
+    missing = "no-such-id"
+    assert backend.call("get_job", {"job_id": missing}) == (
+        f"Error: Job with ID {missing} not found."
+    )
+    assert backend.call("get_job_map", {"job_id": missing}) == (
+        f"Error: Job with ID {missing} not found."
+    )
+    assert backend.call("get_outcomes", {"job_id": missing}) == (
+        f"Error: Job with ID {missing} not found."
+    )
+    assert backend.call("get_step", {"step_id": missing}) == (
+        f"Error: Step with ID {missing} not found."
+    )
+    assert backend.call("get_outcome", {"outcome_id": missing}) == (
+        f"Error: Outcome with ID {missing} not found."
+    )
+    assert backend.call("get_customer_outcome", {"outcome_id": missing}) == (
+        f"Customer outcome not found: {missing}"
+    )
+    assert "Job not found" in backend.call("delete_job", {"job_id": missing})
+    assert "Step with ID" in backend.call("delete_step", {"step_id": missing})
+    assert "Outcome with ID" in backend.call("delete_outcome", {"outcome_id": missing})
+
+
+def test_local_backend_value_out_of_range_messages(tmp_path):
+    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))
+    job_id = _id_from(backend.call("add_job", {"name": "J"}))
+    range_error = "Error: importance and satisfaction must be between 1.0 and 10.0"
+    assert (
+        backend.call("add_outcome", {"job_id": job_id, "statement": "S", "importance": 99.0})
+        == range_error
+    )
+    outcome_id = _id_from(
+        backend.call("add_outcome", {"job_id": job_id, "statement": "S", "importance": 5.0})
+    )
+    assert (
+        backend.call("update_outcome", {"outcome_id": outcome_id, "importance": 99.0})
+        == range_error
+    )
+    assert (
+        backend.call("compute_opportunity", {"importance": 11.0, "satisfaction": 5.0})
+        == range_error
+    )
+    assert (
+        backend.call("compute_opportunity", {"importance": 8.0, "satisfaction": 4.0})
+        == "Opportunity score: 12.00"
+    )
+
+
+def test_local_backend_update_customer_outcome_folds_flat_args(tmp_path):
+    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))
+    job_id = _id_from(backend.call("add_job", {"name": "J"}))
+    created = backend.call(
+        "add_customer_outcome",
+        {
+            "job_id": job_id,
+            "customer_value": {
+                "direction": "minimize",
+                "unit_of_measure": "time",
+                "object_of_control": "setup",
+                "statement": "Minimize setup time",
+                "importance": 5.0,
+                "satisfaction": 5.0,
+            },
+            "business_value": {"category": "cost_reduction", "statement": "Save hours"},
+        },
+    )
+    outcome_id = _id_from(created)
+
+    updated = backend.call(
+        "update_customer_outcome",
+        {
+            "outcome_id": outcome_id,
+            "importance": 7.0,
+            "business_statement": "Save days",
+            "value_metrics": [
+                {
+                    "name": "m2",
+                    "direction": "maximize",
+                    "unit_of_measure": "s",
+                    "importance": 9.0,
+                    "satisfaction": 3.0,
+                }
+            ],
+        },
+    )
+    data = json.loads(re.search(r"({.*})", updated, re.DOTALL).group(1))  # type: ignore[union-attr]
+    assert data["customer_value"]["importance"] == 7.0
+    assert data["customer_value"]["value_metrics"][0]["name"] == "m2"
+    assert data["business_value"]["statement"] == "Save days"
+    assert data["business_value"]["category"] == "cost_reduction"
+
+
+def test_mcp_backend_delegates_to_call_mcp():
+    from unittest.mock import patch
+
+    backend = MCPBackend(mcp_url="http://x/mcp")
+    with patch("cli.backend._call_mcp") as mock_call:
+        mock_call.return_value = "[]"
+        result = backend.call("get_jobs", {})
+    assert result == "[]"
+    mock_call.assert_called_once_with("get_jobs", {}, "http://x/mcp")

+# GitHub Pages Marketing Site Implementation Plan
+
+> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
+
+**Goal:** Ship the single-page GitHub Pages marketing site per the design spec — Jobsian one-pager, quickstart-first CTA, honest experimental framing, reproducible OG art, structural test suite, Actions deploy.
+
+**Architecture:** Static sources in `website/` (`index.html`, `404.html`, `assets/{style.css,main.js,mark.svg,favicon.svg,og.png,favicon.png}`); generator `website/tools/make_og.py` (Pillow, pinned); structural tests in `website/tests/` run from the repo root with the workspace venv; deploy via `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (staged artifact → `deploy-pages`) with a new `website` job added to `ci.yml` and to `ci-green`'s `needs`.
+
+**Tech Stack:** Hand-written HTML/CSS/vanilla JS (no framework, no build step); Python 3.10+ stdlib (`html.parser`, `xml.etree`, `struct`) + pytest for tests; new root dev deps `pillow==12.3.0` (Task 1) and `pyyaml==6.0.3` (Task 4); GitHub Actions `checkout@v7`, `configure-pages@v6`, `upload-pages-artifact@v5`, `deploy-pages@v5`, composite `./.github/actions/setup`; uv.
+
+**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-github-pages-design.md` (copy, tokens, and honesty strings marked binding there are enforced by the tests below)
+
+**Definition of Done:** PR pushed to `main` with **all** GitHub Actions checks green — lint (ruff), typecheck (mypy), security (bandit), tests (pytest ×6 packages + `website`), smoke, and the "CI green" aggregate — touching only files this plan names. Maintainer enables Pages (Source: GitHub Actions) **before merge**, or the post-merge deploy on `main` fails.
+
+## Global Constraints
+
+- Publishable artifact = `website/` minus `tests/` and `tools/`, staged by the workflow with `rsync --exclude tests/ --exclude tools/ website/ _site/`. `_site/` is CI-only; add `/_site` to `.gitignore`. Never commit `_site/`.
+- **Paths:** all in-page refs relative (`assets/…`, `#anchor`); `rel=canonical`, `og:url`, `og:image`, `og:description` absolute to `https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/`. The 404 page is self-contained: zero `link`/`script`/`img` refs, absolute home link.
+- **Root lint config (Task 1):** add to root `pyproject.toml` — `[tool.ruff] line-length = 100`, `target-version = "py310"`; `[tool.ruff.lint] select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "BLE"]` (mirrors `cli/pyproject.toml`). Verified: no root-level `.py` files exist besides the new `website/**`, so existing files keep their package configs. `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` (run in CI from root) now cover `website/**` — run both before every commit.
+- **Dev deps:** root `[dependency-groups] dev` gains `pillow==12.3.0` (Task 1) and `pyyaml==6.0.3` (Task 4), each followed by `uv lock`; CI's `uv sync --all-packages --locked` must stay satisfiable. `website/**` stays **outside** mypy and bandit scopes — do not edit those CI commands.
+- **Tests:** run from repo root as `uv run pytest website/tests -q`. No network in tests. Tests never write outside `tmp_path` — the committed PNGs are read-only; regenerate them only via `uv run python website/tools/make_og.py`.
+- **Copy contract (enforced):** `Experimental`; `requires a free Prefect account`; `All rights reserved`; `as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)`; `http://localhost:8000/mcp`; `http://localhost:8501`; quickstart verbatim from README (`uv sync --all-packages`, `python -m client.run`); headline `Your roadmap is a guess.`; opportunity formula exactly `Opportunity = Importance + max(Importance − Satisfaction, 0)`. No milestone dates (a © year is the only year allowed). No emoji. No `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app`, no Discord, no `mailto:`.
+- **External link allowlist (closed set):** `https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi`, `https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/issues`, `https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat`, `https://docs.astral.sh/uv/`, `https://modelcontextprotocol.io`, canonical Pages URL.
+- **Design system:** tokens per spec's color table (both schemes via `prefers-color-scheme`, all text pairs ≥ 4.5:1); system font stacks only — no webfonts; code blocks dark in both schemes. JS ≤ 100 non-blank lines, `defer`, progressive enhancement (content visible without JS), `prefers-reduced-motion` honored.
+- Scope discipline: no changes to package source, no edits to `docs/` (this spec/plan excepted), README edited only in Task 5, no new workspace members.
+
+## Review Focus
+
+Uncovered inputs/conditions most likely to bite a user — each has a test in the task that owns the code:
+
+1. **Dead anchors or base-path breakage** — relative refs + closed allowlist + resource-existence checks; site must work under the `/agentic-odi/` base. (Task 2)
+2. **Committed PNG drifting from its generator** — pixel-identity test fails until the art is regenerated (regenerate with the pinned Pillow in the project venv; FreeType ships inside Pillow wheels, so output matches across platforms). (Task 1)
+3. **Dev files published to Pages** — artifact staging excludes `tests/` + `tools/`; workflow contract test pins it. (Task 4)
+4. **Honesty regressions** — no milestone dates, required strings, formula ↔ `core/models.py`, README ↔ page command drift. (Tasks 2, 5)
+5. **JS-off / reduced-motion / scheme failures** — reveal must never hide content without JS; both schemes legible. (Task 3)
+6. **Root lint newly covers `website/**`** — ruff check + format parity before every commit. (Tasks 1–5)
+7. **Pages source not enabled before merge** — deploy job on `main` fails until the manual toggle; must be done pre-merge. (Task 6)
+
+---
+
+### Task 1: OG image generator + committed social art
+
+**Files:**
+- Modify: `pyproject.toml` (root dev deps + `[tool.ruff]`), `uv.lock`
+- Create: `website/tools/make_og.py`, `website/assets/og.png`, `website/assets/favicon.png`
+- Test: `website/tests/test_make_og.py`
+
+**Interfaces:**
+- Consumes: `pillow==12.3.0` (new root dev dep); design tokens from the spec (canvas `#0b0d13`, surface `#131722`, text `#f1f5f9`, muted `#94a3b8`, accent `#409cff`, badge fg `#cbd5e1`).
+- Produces (importable via `importlib.util` from the tests; also runnable as `uv run python website/tools/make_og.py`):
+  - `make_og.OG_SIZE = (1200, 630)`, `make_og.FAVICON_SIZE = (32, 32)`
+  - `make_og.DEFAULT_HEADLINE = "Your roadmap is a guess."`, `DEFAULT_SUBHEAD = "Verified customer outcomes, jobs, and opportunity scores — served over MCP."`, `DEFAULT_URL = "alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi"`
+  - `make_og.render(headline: str = DEFAULT_HEADLINE, subhead: str = DEFAULT_SUBHEAD, url: str = DEFAULT_URL) -> bytes` — PNG bytes of the 1200×630 card: dark canvas, hairline rounded frame, mark (rounded-square + ascending two-step polyline + apex dot) with "Agentic ODI" wordmark top-left, "Experimental" pill top-right, headline wrapped ≤ 2 lines, subhead muted beneath, URL bottom-left. Font: `ImageFont.load_default(size=…)` (Pillow-embedded Aileron — no font file). No timestamps, fixed positions, `compress_level=9, optimize=True` → deterministic bytes.

+You write release notes for Agentic ODI, aimed at the person who installs and uses the product — never at developers.
+
+# Input
+You receive one JSON manifest: every commit in this release (full SHA, subject, body, parsed type/scope/breaking, changed files). It is the only information you may use.
+
+# Rules
+1. Use ONLY facts present in the manifest. Never invent features, product names, versions, file paths, numbers, or benefits that the commits do not support.
+2. Write plain-language, value-focused sentences: one sentence per entry, ideally under 200 characters. Never quote commit subjects verbatim; no scopes, branch names, PR numbers, jargon, exclamation marks, or emoji.
+3. Group entries under exactly these section names and omit empty ones: "Initial release" (only when manifest.initial is true), "Added", "Improved", "Fixed", "Security", "Removed". Keep this order.

+6. Do not create entries for chore, ci, build, test, docs, style, or dependency-bump commits unless the commit clearly describes a user benefit. Put refactor commits under "Improved" only when the commit states a user-visible benefit.
+7. Set "breaking": true for entries summarizing a breaking commit and start that entry's text with "Breaking change: ".
+8. Output ONLY one JSON object, no prose and no code fences, with exactly this shape:
+{"schema_version": 1, "version": "...", "previous_version": "... or null", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "generated_by": "ai", "generator": {"model": "...", "prompt_version": "1"}, "disclosure": "This changelog was generated with AI from our release history.", "sections": [{"name": "Added", "entries": [{"text": "...", "sources": ["<40-char sha>"], "breaking": false}]}]}

+# GitHub Pages Marketing Site Design
+
+**Date:** 2026-10-18
+**Status:** Approved (design authority delegated to the session designer; all builder-check questions answered)
+**Scope:** Single-page customer-facing site in `website/` + GitHub Actions deploy to GitHub Pages
+
+## Intent & Why
+
+`README.md` is the project's front door, and it reads like an engineering changelog — right for
+contributors, wrong for the PM or eng lead who clicked a shared link asking "is this real, and is it
+worth five minutes?" The site answers why/what/how/when in one scroll, with a Jobsian bar:
+ruthless focus, one narrative, one obvious action, craft in type and motion, and honesty as the
+brand — the project is an experimental testbed, and the page says so out loud.
+
+The Jobsian constraint that shapes everything: **over-promising on an experimental product is the
+one thing Jobs never did — the honest answer is the Jobsian answer.** No dates, no maturity theater,
+no CTAs that dead-end behind auth, no screenshots of vaporware.
+
+Definition of done for the build (see plan): PR pushed with all GitHub Actions checks green —
+lint (ruff), typecheck (mypy), security (bandit), tests (pytest ×6 packages + `website`), smoke,
+and the "CI green" aggregate.
+
+## Audience & Jobs-to-be-Done
+
+**Primary — product managers / innovation leads.** Landing cold from a shared link, a search, or a
+referral. Skeptical of AI-tool marketing.
+> When I open this page from a link in Slack, I want to know within one screen whether this is a
+> real, runnable thing grounded in a method I respect, so I can decide to spend five minutes on it
+> or leave without guilt.
+
+**Secondary — AI/agent developers.** Evaluating whether to wire agents to an ODI data source.
+> When I'm deciding what context to give my agents, I want the exact endpoint and a copy-paste
+> quickstart that works locally, so I can try it without talking to anyone.
+
+**Tertiary — the sharing PM (internal champion).** Forwarding the link to a team or a boss.
+> When I forward this page, I want it to frame the thesis — evidence over opinion — credibly and
+> soberly, so the conversation starts from the idea instead of from my credibility.
+
+## Messaging Hierarchy
+
+Binding copy contract (tests enforce the marked strings; micro-polish — punctuation-level tweaks —
+is builder latitude).
+
+| Level | Copy |
+|---|---|
+| Eyebrow pill | `Experimental` |
+| H1 (hero) | **Your roadmap is a guess.** |
+| Hero sub | An MCP server that hands your agents verified customer outcomes — and the evidence behind them. |
+| Primary CTA | **Run it in 60 seconds** → `#run` (local quickstart) |
+| Secondary CTA | View on GitHub → `https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi` |
+| Tertiary link | Hosted demo — requires a free Prefect account → Horizon chat URL |
+| Footer tagline | Built with outcomes, not guesses. |
+
+**Section 2 — `#problem`, "Opinion is expensive."** Three parallel beats, one line each, each with
+a short support line:
+
+1. "Roadmaps set by whoever talks loudest." — Decisions default to seniority, not evidence.
+2. "Features for customers who never asked." — Nobody validated the outcome; only the idea.
+3. "Agents fluent in everything, grounded in nothing." — A model will confidently invent your customer.
+
+Section closer: "Add it up and the roadmap isn't a plan. It's a guess."
+
+**Section 3 — `#insight`, "Ask for outcomes, not opinions."** Three plain sentences:
+1. Outcome-Driven Innovation asks customers how much each desired outcome matters and how satisfied
+   they are with it today.
+2. The gap between importance and satisfaction is where products win or die.
+3. Agentic ODI stores those outcomes, scores them, and serves them to any agent over MCP.
+
+Then: a small CSS/inline-SVG bar visual (Importance vs Satisfaction, gap highlighted, labeled
+"Illustrative outcome data"), the formula rendered exactly as the code computes it —
+`Opportunity = Importance + max(Importance − Satisfaction, 0)` (source of truth:
+`core/src/core/models.py:27`), and the stat callout: **86%** innovation success rate — *as reported
+in ODI literature (Strategyn)*. Plain-text attribution only; no link to the in-repo PDF.
+
+**Section 4 — `#how`, "How it works."** Three steps:
+1. **Capture** — jobs, steps, and desired outcomes with importance/satisfaction scores, via CLI,
+   connectors, or The Living Studio.
+2. **Query** — agents call MCP tools for job maps and opportunity scores at decision time, local or
+   hosted.
+3. **Steer** — The Living Studio shows the Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, and Impact
+   Simulation so the team decides from the same picture.
+
+Accompanies: a stylized Studio illustration (real shipped surfaces, marked "Illustrative"), never a
+fake screenshot.
+
+**Section 5 — `#run`, "Run it in 60 seconds."** Prerequisites line (Python 3.10+, uv), terminal
+block with copy button:
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi.git
+cd agentic-odi
+uv sync --all-packages
+python -m client.run
+```
+
+Endpoint chips with copy buttons: MCP `http://localhost:8000/mcp` · Studio `http://localhost:8501`.
+MCP client config snippet (local only):
+
+```json
+{
+  "mcpServers": {
+    "agentic-odi": { "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Prose note: hosted credentials come from the maintainers — open an issue. Never invent an auth
+scheme we cannot document.
+
+**Section 6 — `#status`, "Honest status."** `Experimental` badge; **What works today** (MCP server
+tools for jobs/steps/outcomes/customer outcomes with opportunity scoring; The Living Studio —
+Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, Impact Simulation, Causal Lineage; CLI `outcomes` +
+`connectors`; MCP ingest connector; hosted test endpoints requiring auth) and **What's next**
+(curated from the README roadmap at build time: map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts, more
+connector kinds, ODI schema definition, context tooling, persistence layer, agentic integration).
+Standing line: "We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does." Closer: "Questions?
+Open an issue." → Issues link.
+
+**Footer.** Mark + wordmark, tagline, links (GitHub, Issues, Hosted demo), legal line:
+`© 2026 Agentic ODI maintainers · All rights reserved` + one-line experimental reminder.
+
+**Voice rules:** warm, direct, second person; plain language; no jargon dumps; **no emoji anywhere
+on the site** (house copy rule from the first-run onboarding spec — README's emoji style stays in
+README); no superlatives ("revolutionary", "seamless", "enterprise-grade"); English only.
+
+## Information Architecture / Sitemap
+
+| Route | File | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| `/` | `website/index.html` | The entire site. One scroll, seven sections. |
+| `/404.html` | `website/404.html` | On-brand, **self-contained** (inline styles, absolute link home) so it renders at any depth on project Pages. |
+
+- Sticky compact header: mark + wordmark (left), single CTA "Run it in 60 seconds" (right). No nav
+  links — one page needs no navigation, but the one obvious action must stay reachable.
+- In-page anchors: `#problem`, `#insight`, `#how`, `#run`, `#status`.
+- No sitemap.xml, no robots.txt, no blog, no docs pages, no search.
+
+## Visual Direction
+
+**Type.** No webfonts, zero downloads:
+- `--font-sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif`
+  (same stack The Living Studio ships, `client/src/client/app.py:36`)
+- `--font-mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`
+
+| Role | Size | Weight / tracking |
+|---|---|---|
+| H1 | `clamp(2.75rem, 6.5vw, 4.75rem)` | 700, `-0.02em`, lh 1.05 |
+| H2 | `clamp(1.75rem, 3.2vw, 2.5rem)` | 700, `-0.015em`, lh 1.15 |
+| H3 / beats | `1.25rem` | 600, lh 1.3 |
+| Body / lead | `1.0625rem` (17px) / `1.1875rem` | 400, lh 1.6 |
+| Eyebrow, badges | `0.75rem` | 600, `0.08em`, uppercase |
+| Code | `0.9375rem` mono | lh 1.55 |
+
+**Color.** Tokens as CSS custom properties; `:root` = light, `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`
+overrides. Palette echoes the shipped Studio dark-glass theme (`#0B0D13` / `#131722` / `#F1F5F9`
+straight from `app.py`). All ratios measured, WCAG 2.1 AA (text ≥ 4.5:1):
+

+|---|---|---|---|

+
+Code blocks are dark (`#0b0d13`) in both schemes — a terminal is a terminal (17.7:1 either way).
+OG card is fixed dark, self-contained.
+
+**Layout & spacing.** Mobile-first; content max-width 1080px, prose max-width 68ch; inline padding
+`clamp(20px, 5vw, 40px)`; section padding-block `clamp(72px, 12vw, 140px)`; 8px spacing scale as
+custom properties; radius 12px cards / 999px pills (echoing the Studio's own radii); 1px hairline
+borders. Beats and steps go two-column at ≥720px.
+
+**Motion.** Restrained, explanatory, never load-bearing:
+- Hero stagger on load: eyebrow → H1 → sub → CTAs, 12px fade-up, 60ms stagger, 400ms,
+  `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)` — pure CSS, no JS.
+- Scroll reveal: sections fade-up once when 15% visible (IntersectionObserver). Default state is
+  **visible**; JS opts content into the hidden-then-reveal state only after it loads, so no-JS
+  readers never see hidden content.
+- Buttons: 150ms `background-color`/`transform`, hover `translateY(-1px)`, active `scale(.98)`.
+- Copy button swaps its label to "Copied" for 1.5s, announced via an `aria-live="polite"` span.
+- `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`: all transforms/stagger removed, reveals off, content
+  immediate.
+
+**Imagery & assets (none exist in the repo — all created):**

+  upward. Accent stroke `#0071e3`, hairline frame. Works at 16px, single color-safe.

+## Technical Approach
+
+Hand-crafted static HTML + one CSS file + ≤100 lines of vanilla JS. **No framework** (no
+Astro/Next/React): one page with no routing, no state, no data, no components shared across
+views — a framework buys a toolchain, a lockfile, hydration, and an upgrade treadmill, and charges
+rent on every one of them. Consequence of no framework: deploy is "copy files", the review diff is
+readable HTML, Lighthouse is high by construction, and there is zero supply chain on the page.
+
+```
+website/
+  index.html            # the site
+  404.html              # self-contained fallback
+  assets/
+    style.css           # tokens + full design system (no external URLs)
+    main.js             # ≤100 lines: reveal + copy buttons, defer, progressive enhancement
+    mark.svg  favicon.svg
+    og.png    favicon.png   # committed, generated (see OG strategy)
+  tools/
+    make_og.py          # regenerates og.png + favicon.png (Pillow, pinned)
+  tests/
+    test_site.py  test_assets.py  test_make_og.py
+    test_workflows.py  test_readme_sync.py
+```
+
+- **Paths:** every in-page URL is **relative** (`assets/…`, `#anchor`) so the site works under the
+  project-Pages base `/agentic-odi/`, on a local static server, and on any future custom domain.
+  `og:url` / `og:image` / `rel=canonical` are **absolute**.
+- Local preview: `python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory website` (preview the 404 by opening
+  `/404.html` directly — `http.server` serves its own 404).
+- JS is `defer`'d and additive: the page is complete, styled, and readable with JS disabled.
+- Python tooling lives only in `tools/` + `tests/`, run from the repo root with the workspace venv.
+
+## OG / Social Strategy
+
+Social previews are the main earned-distribution artifact — one committed raster, no mystery binary.
+
+- `website/assets/og.png`: **1200×630**, fixed dark card — mark + "Agentic ODI" wordmark,
+  headline "Your roadmap is a guess.", sub "Verified customer outcomes, jobs, and opportunity
+  scores — served over MCP.", bottom row `alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi` + Experimental badge.
+- `website/tools/make_og.py`: the committed, runnable generator (stdlib argparse + Pillow). Writes
+  `og.png` and `favicon.png`; defaults embed the canonical card copy above. Deterministic output —
+  fixed palette/positions, no timestamps, `compress_level=9`, font via
+  `ImageFont.load_default(size=…)` (Pillow's embedded Aileron, SIL OFL — no font file in the repo).
+  Run: `uv run python website/tools/make_og.py`.
+- **Regenerability is enforced:** `test_make_og.py` renders fresh bytes and asserts they are
+  pixel-identical to the committed PNGs. Change the script → the test fails until you regenerate.
+  Change the card copy → defaults in the script are the source.
+- Meta contract on `index.html`: `og:type=website`, `og:site_name`, `og:title`
+  ("Your roadmap is a guess. — Agentic ODI"), `og:description`, `og:url` (canonical Pages URL),
+  `og:image` (absolute PNG URL), `twitter:card=summary_large_image` + title/description/image,
+  `rel=canonical`, `theme-color` per color scheme, both favicons. Title tag ≤ 60 chars:
+  `Agentic ODI — Ground agents in verified customer outcomes`.
+- og:image is never loaded by the page itself (page weight unaffected).
+- No OpenGraph on SVG: scrapers (X, LinkedIn, Slack, iMessage) need raster — hence exactly one PNG.
+
+## Deploy Pipeline
+
+**`.github/workflows/pages.yml`** (deploy only — its contract is tested in `ci.yml` via
+`test_workflows.py`, so PRs validate it without triggering a deploy):
+
+- `on: push branches [main] paths [website/**, .github/workflows/pages.yml]`, plus
+  `workflow_dispatch`.
+- Workflow permissions: `contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`. Concurrency:
+  `group: pages`, `cancel-in-progress: false`. Environment: `github-pages` (URL from the
+  deployment step).
+- Job `deploy`, steps: checkout@v7 → `./.github/actions/setup` → **run
+  `uv run pytest website/tests -q` (verify before publish)** → `actions/configure-pages@v6` →
+  stage the artifact with
+  `mkdir -p _site && rsync -a --exclude tests/ --exclude tools/ website/ _site/` →
+  `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5` (`path: _site`) → `actions/deploy-pages@v5`.
+  Only the site publishes — tests and generator never do; `_site/` is CI-only and gitignored.
+- **Manual gate:** repository Settings → Pages → Source = "GitHub Actions" must be set **before
+  this workflow first runs on `main`**, or the deploy job fails. (One-time toggle; flag before
+  merge.)
+
+**`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: add a `website` job (setup + `uv run pytest website/tests -q`,
+timeout 10m) and add `website` to `ci-green`'s `needs`. Root `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .`
+already cover `website/**` once root ruff config exists (below).
+
+## Accessibility & Performance Budget
+
+**Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA):**
+- Semantic landmarks (`header`/`main`/`footer`), one `h1`, no skipped heading levels, `lang="en"`.
+- Contrast: measured pairs in the color table — every text pair ≥ 4.5:1 in both schemes.
+- Full keyboard operability; visible focus ring (≥ 3:1 against adjacent colors); copy controls are
+  real `<button>`s with accessible names; `aria-live` for "Copied".
+- Decorative SVG `aria-hidden="true"`; meaningful links (no "click here"); `prefers-reduced-motion`
+  respected; viewport meta; tested at 360px width with no horizontal scroll.
+
+**Performance:**
+- Zero third-party requests, zero webfonts, zero analytics, zero cookies — the page talks only to
+  its own origin.
+- Weights (raw, committed): HTML ≤ 60 KB, CSS ≤ 30 KB, JS ≤ 4 KB (≤ 100 non-blank lines), each SVG
+  ≤ 10 KB, `favicon.png` ≤ 5 KB, total transferred ≤ 150 KB; `og.png` ≤ 300 KB (test-enforced;
+  expected ~15–40 KB).
+- Lighthouse ≥ 95 on Performance / Accessibility / Best Practices / SEO (mobile emulation,
+  manual run before merge — CI has no browser).
+
+## Non-Goals / Anti-Goals
+
+- **Not a docs site, not a blog.** No MkDocs/Docusaurus, no nav maze, no search, no sitemap.
+- **No framework, no build step, no dependencies on the deployed artifact.**
+- **No claims the repo can't back:** no dates or milestones; no "open source" or license claim
+  (repo is all-rights-reserved); no maturity language beyond the Experimental framing; no invented
+  testimonials, logos, customer counts, or benchmark numbers; no emoji.
+- **No dead ends:** no CTAs behind auth (hosted is tertiary, labeled); no personal emails, no
+  invented Discord/Slack; access channel = GitHub Issues only.
+- **No auth fiction:** local MCP config only; never link the 401 `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app`
+  endpoint as something a visitor can try; no invented header/token scheme.
+- **No vaporware imagery:** Studio illustration is abstraction-of-shipped-surfaces, labeled
+  "Illustrative"; no fake screenshots.
+- **No hotlinking `knowledge/Strategyn_*.pdf`** — attribution text only.
+- **No analytics/cookies/CDN/fonts/i18n** — scope is English, one page, two schemes.
+- **No publishing dev files:** `website/tests/` and `website/tools/` never reach the Pages artifact.
+
+## Risks & Mitigations
+
+1. **Pages not enabled before first merge** → deploy job red on `main`. Mitigation: manual toggle
+   flagged as a pre-merge gate in the plan's final task.
+2. **README drift** (commands/URLs change, page rots) → `test_readme_sync.py` fails CI.
+3. **Committed PNG drifts from generator** → pixel-identity test fails CI until regeneration.
+4. **Scope creep** (nav items, extra pages, webfonts) → anti-goals + structural tests (allowlisted
+   links, weight budgets) push back mechanically.
+5. **Ruff newly covers `website/**`** → root config added at repo-consistent line length; commit
+   steps run root lint/format parity before every commit.
+
+## Resolved Questions (builder-check × session — all settled)
+
+1. **Primary CTA** → local quickstart ("Run it in 60 seconds"). Verified live: Horizon chat 302s
+   to `auth.horizon.prefect.io`, hosted MCP returns 401 — a hero CTA that dead-ends anonymous
+   visitors in auth is malpractice. Hosted is tertiary, labeled "requires a free Prefect account."
+2. **Access channel** → GitHub Issues (footer + status section). No personal email, no invented
+   Discord.
+3. **MCP snippet** → local config only (`http://localhost:8000/mcp`); hosted credentials are
+   requested via issues. Never document an auth scheme we don't have.
+4. **OG image** → one committed PNG, regenerated by committed `website/tools/make_og.py`
+   (deterministic, tested pixel-identical). SVG-only cards render poorly on X/LinkedIn/iMessage.
+5. **"When"** → no dates. "What works today / What's next" under an explicit Experimental badge,
+   mirroring the README roadmap.
+6. **Living Studio visual** → stylized abstraction grounded in real shipped surfaces, labeled
+   "Illustrative" — never a fake screenshot.
+7. **86% stat** → plain-text attribution "as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)"; no link to
+   the copyrighted in-repo PDF.
+
+## Builder Calls (design authority — beyond the session's settled six)
+
+1. **Formula corrected to repo truth:** the session sketch showed `Opportunity = Importance −
+   Satisfaction`; the code computes `importance + max(importance − satisfaction, 0)`
+   (`core/src/core/models.py:28`). The page shows the real formula, and a test pins page ↔ code.
+2. **OG renderer = Pillow, pinned in root dev deps** (`pillow==12.3.0`, `uv.lock` updated):
+   `ImageFont.load_default(size=…)` ships the Aileron font inside Pillow — real typography, no font
+   binary, deterministic bytes, zero deploy-time dependency (Pillow never ships to Pages).
+   Generator also emits `favicon.png`.
+3. **Full color/type/motion system specified with measured contrast ratios** (table above); palette
+   lifted from the shipped Studio theme for brand continuity.
+4. **Sticky compact header** (wordmark + one CTA), no nav links.
+5. **`404.html` included, self-contained** — absolute home link + inline styles, because relative
+   assets break when Pages serves 404.html at arbitrary depths under the `/agentic-odi/` base.
+6. **Relative assets + absolute canonical/OG URLs** — required by GitHub project-Pages base path.
+7. **Test/CI architecture:** `website/tests/` run by a new `website` job in `ci.yml` (added to
+   `ci-green` needs) *and* as a verify-before-publish step inside the Pages deploy job; workflow
+   YAML itself is contract-tested with PyYAML (`pyyaml==6.0.3` declared in root dev deps).
+8. **Artifact staging** via `rsync --exclude tests/ --exclude tools/` → `_site/` (CI-only,
+   gitignored): the published site is the site, nothing else.
+9. **Root `[tool.ruff]` added** (line-length 100, target py310, select `E4,E7,E9,F,I,UP,B,BLE`,
+   mirroring `cli/pyproject.toml`) so `website/**` Python is linted at repo standards — verified
+   impact is website-only (no other root-level `.py` files exist).
+10. **Hosted link = Horizon chat only**; the `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app` endpoint is never linked
+    (401) — it is mentioned only as "credentials via an issue."
+11. **Closed external-link allowlist** (repo, Issues, Horizon chat, uv docs, MCP docs, canonical);
+    no analytics, no sitemap/robots/JSON-LD — SEO comes from meta + structure alone.
+12. **No emoji on the site** (README's emoji vocabulary stays in README).
+13. **Pages source toggle is a pre-merge gate**, not a post-merge note — without it `main` goes red.
+
+## What's Left to the Builder
+
+Exact micro-copy polish within the binding strings above; section/illustration composition and grid
+details; animation timing fine-tuning within the stated curves; favicon/mark geometry drafting within
+the stated concept; breakpoint tuning; workflow YAML details not specified (names, step ordering).

+# User-Facing Auto-Generated Changelog — Design
+
+**Date:** 2026-10-18
+**Status:** Approved (design session `ses_ebea76e4dffeNzxhwoqkB40AW5`, user decisions binding)
+**Scope:** Release-time AI changelog generation with grounding guardrails, GitHub Release delivery, `odi changelog` CLI surface, commit/branch/semver standard + enforcement
+
+## Intent & Why
+
+When a user updates agentic-odi — or decides whether to — they need one thing: a complete, plain-language account of what changed **since the version they last ran**, so they can judge the value and act. Today there is no changelog at all: no tags, no release notes, and PR #8's release-please config would commit a developer-facing `CHANGELOG.md` that (a) is written in commit-speak, not user language, and (b) is a merge-conflict magnet.
+
+Jobsian bar: the user never reads a commit. They type one command (`odi changelog`) — or see one hint line after an upgrade — and get professionally written, value-focused entries that cover **every user-visible change** in their gap, each provably grounded in the actual release commits (no hallucination), with an honest AI disclaimer. Fully automated end to end; the guardrails, not a human gate, are the safety mechanism.
+
+## User-Facing Audience & Voice
+
+- **Audience:** the person who installs/uses agentic-odi (not contributors, not release engineers).
+- **Voice:** professionally written, value-focused, second person, no developer-speak. Never show branch names, scopes, PR numbers, raw commit subjects, or SHAs in the default view (SHAs exist only as machine-readable citations in `changelog.json`).
+- **Example of the rewrite we expect:**
+  - Commit: `fix(cli): require Python 3.11 to match StrEnum usage`
+  - Entry: `Fixed startup on machines running Python 3.11 or newer.`
+- Every entry answers "what do I gain?" — new capability, improved behavior, or a fix I'd care about.
+
+## Goals
+
+1. Auto-generated user-facing changelog, produced **at release time**, included **in the release** (body + asset), never as a committed source file.
+2. Complete coverage: every user-visible change since the user's last seen version appears — no gaps, no silent drops.
+3. Grounded AI rewrite: structured output with per-entry commit-SHA citations, validated fail-closed against the commit range (no hallucinated SHAs, features, versions, or identifiers).
+4. AI disclaimer on every release and in `changelog.json`.
+5. Conventional Commits + Conventional Branches + semver tags enforced (standard + tooling), so the generator has reliable input.
+6. Minimal runtime surface: `odi changelog [--since VERSION] [--all] [--json]`, fetching notes from GitHub Releases; GUI (Streamlit client) reuses the same core module later.
+
+## Non-Goals / Anti-Goals
+
+- **No committed `CHANGELOG.md`** — this supersedes PR #8's release-please default behavior (`skip-changelog: true`; see "Release workflow integration").
+- No raw commit-log dump presented to users; no developer changelog as the user-facing artifact.
+- No LLM call in the shipped CLI/GUI — generation is release-time only; runtime only fetches and renders.
+- No routine human review step in the release happy path ("fully automated" honored); humans are involved only when a guardrail trips (fail-closed draft) or during recovery.
+- No requirement that contributors write user-facing prose in commits (the AI owns the rewrite).
+- No bundling full release history into the binary; no i18n scope; no per-commit entries for hidden commit classes.
+
+## The Standard (input quality)
+
+### Commits — Conventional Commits
+
+`type(scope): subject`, optional `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
+
+- Types: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`, `style`.
+- Scopes: package names (`cli`, `client`, `connectors`, `core`, `mcp_server`, `local_server`) plus `ci`, `deps`, `release`, `workspace`.
+- PR titles must follow the same form (squash merges make the PR title the commit on `main`).
+- Enforcement: `core.convention` module → pre-commit `commit-msg` hook (local), CI `convention` job (PR title on `pull_request`, head-commit subject on `push`; merge commits exempt).
+
+### Branches — Conventional Branch
+
+Allowed prefixes (kebab-case, single level): `feature/`, `fix/`, `hotfix/`, `chore/`, `docs/`, `refactor/`, `test/`, `release/`, and `topic/` (documented legacy alias of `feature/`, from the project's existing `topic/*` habit). Exempt from checks: `main`, `dependabot/*`, `renovate/*`, `release-please*`, `worktree/*`, `superpowers/*`. Enforced in CI on every PR head ref (no local branch hook — documented convention only).
+
+### Tags / semver
+
+`vX.Y.Z`. Breaking → major, `feat` → minor, else patch; **`bump-minor-pre-major: true`** (pre-1.0 breaking changes bump minor, not jump to 1.0). Engine: **release-please** (kept from PR #8 — see reconcilation below).
+
+### What "complete" honestly means
+
+- **Coverage-required** (must be cited by ≥1 entry or validation fails): types `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `revert`, and any commit with `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:`.
+- **Hidden from users** (never required; omitted unless clearly user-value-bearing): `chore`, `ci`, `build`, `test`, `docs`, `style`, and `deps` (a `chore(deps)` scope). Their omission is not a gap — they are not changes *to the user's product*.
+- **Eligible but optional**: `refactor` (AI may surface it under Improved when the commit states a user benefit; absence never fails validation).
+- **Exempt**: merge commits (excluded from the manifest entirely) and commits whose subject doesn't parse as conventional (the pre-standard legacy minority — 13 of 64 today). "Complete" = complete over changes **expressed in the standard**; legacy commits may be surfaced opportunistically but are not gateable.
+
+## Data Pipeline
+
+```
+commits on main (Conventional Commits, squash-merged)
+        │
+        ▼
+release-please  ──►  Release PR (semver decision) ──merge──►  tag vX.Y.Z
+        │                                                      + DRAFT GitHub Release
+        │ chained job (same workflow, output-gated on releases_created=true)
+        ▼
+① manifest:  git log prev-tag..tag  (sha, subject, body≤600c, type/scope/breaking, files≤50)
+        ▼
+② AI rewrite: pinned model, temperature 0, JSON-mode, prompt = docs-in-repo prompt.md
+        ▼
+③ guardrails: schema + cited-SHA existence + coverage + grounding checks (fail-closed, exit 2)
+        ▼
+④ emit:      changelog.json (schema-validated) + changelog.md (release body) + manifest.json (audit)
+        ▼
+⑤ publish:   gh release upload changelog.json  →  gh release edit --notes-file changelog.md --draft=false
+              (any failure above ⇒ release stays a draft; nothing broken ships half-annotated)
+        │
+        ▼
+release.yml (PR #8) builds binaries & attaches assets
+        │
+        ▼
+runtime:  odi changelog  ──fetch──►  GitHub Releases API  ──►  changelog.json assets
+          since last-seen version ► rendered plain-language "What's new" + AI disclosure
+```
+
+Delivery is **fetch-from-GitHub-Releases** (user decision): the binary stays lean; the CLI (and later the Streamlit GUI) computes the gap between the last version whose notes were shown and the installed version.
+
+## Grounding Guardrails Spec
+
+### 1. Source material (the only ground truth)
+
+The manifest is built exclusively from git: for each non-merge commit in `prev_tag..tag` (or full history in initial mode): full 40-char SHA, subject, body (truncated to 600 chars), parsed `type`/`scope`/`breaking` (or `null`), and up to 50 changed file paths. No PR descriptions, no web content, no prior changelog text enters the prompt.
+
+### 2. Generation contract
+
+- Provider-agnostic OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint; env: `AGENTIC_ODI_CHANGELOG_MODEL` (required), `AGENTIC_ODI_CHANGELOG_BASE_URL` (default `https://api.openai.com/v1`), `AGENTIC_ODI_CHANGELOG_API_KEY` (required online).
+- `temperature: 0`, `response_format: {"type": "json_object"}`, prompt pinned in `scripts/changelog/prompt.md` with a `prompt_version` constant (bump when prompt changes).
+- Prompt rules: end-user voice; only manifest information; every entry cites ≥1 source SHA (full); one sentence per entry (≤ ~200 chars); section vocabulary fixed; cover every coverage-required commit; `breaking` flag set for `!` commits; output only JSON.
+
+### 3. Validation (fail-closed — exit code 2, release stays draft)
+
+| # | Rule | Tier |
+|---|------|------|
+| G1 | Response parses as JSON and matches the schema (`changelog.json` shape) | hard |
+| G2 | Every cited SHA resolves to a manifest commit (≥7-char prefix of a real SHA in range) | hard |
+| G3 | Every entry has ≥1 citation; every section non-empty; ≥1 entry total | hard |
+| G4 | Every coverage-required manifest commit is cited by ≥1 entry | hard |
+| G5 | Section names ∈ {Initial release, Added, Improved, Fixed, Security, Removed} | hard |
+| G6a | "Risky" tokens in entry text must appear in manifest text: backtick spans, `snake_case`, file paths with extensions, `x.y.z` version numbers | hard |
+| G6b | `SCREAMING_CASE` tokens not found in manifest | soft (warn only) |
+
+G6b is deliberately soft: acronyms like JTBD/MCP are common prose and a false positive must not block a release. G6a is hard: backticked code, snake identifiers, paths, and version numbers are exactly where hallucination would do damage.
+
+**Reconciliation with "fully automated":** the happy path requires zero human touch. The safety mechanism is the fail-closed draft — generation/validation failure leaves the release as an unpublished draft with a red Actions run; the runbook (CONTRIBUTING) covers recovery (fix & rerun, or regenerate locally and attach manually). No prose review gate on every release.
+
+**Audit trail:** `manifest.json` + the raw model response are uploaded as workflow artifacts (90 days) so any entry can be traced to its sources after the fact.
+
+### 4. Disclaimer
+
+Constant, used in the CLI footer and appended to every release body:
+
+> This changelog was generated with AI from our release history.
+
+`changelog.json` also carries `"generated_by": "ai"` and `generator: {model, prompt_version}`.
+
+## Output Schema
+
+`changelog.json` (one asset per release; the machine-readable contract for CLI/GUI):
+
+```json
+{
+  "schema_version": 1,
+  "version": "0.2.0",
+  "previous_version": "0.1.0",
+  "date": "2026-10-18",
+  "generated_by": "ai",
+  "generator": { "model": "<pinned model id>", "prompt_version": "1" },
+  "disclosure": "This changelog was generated with AI from our release history.",
+  "sections": [
+    { "name": "Added",
+      "entries": [
+        { "text": "Write outcome updates from the local server.",
+          "sources": ["<full 40-char sha>", "..."],
+          "breaking": false }
+      ] }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+- `previous_version`: `null` for the initial release. `date`: UTC `YYYY-MM-DD`.
+- `sources` are builder details: SHAs tying every sentence to the commits it came from; hidden from default rendering, shown in `--json`.
+- Release body (markdown) = per-section `### Section` + `- text` bullets (`- **Breaking change:** text` when flagged), blank line, italic disclosure. No SHAs in prose.
+
+## Release Workflow Integration (reconciling with PR #8)
+
+PR #8 (release-please + self-update) is the semver/tag authority and stays. It is amended, not replaced:
+
+1. `release-please-config.json` (package `.`) gains:
+   - `"skip-changelog": true` — release-please never writes a `CHANGELOG.md` (dissolves the merge-conflict concern; `.release-please-manifest.json` remains a tiny, conflict-light version marker, not a changelog).
+   - `"draft": true` + `"force-tag-creation": true` — releases are born drafts (GitHub doesn't tag drafts until publish; `force-tag-creation` makes the tag immediately so ranges resolve).
+   - `"bump-minor-pre-major": true`.
+2. `.github/workflows/release-please.yml` gains a chained `changelog` job (`needs: release-please`, `if: releases_created == 'true'`, step `id: release-please`): checkout `fetch-depth: 0` → `generate.py --tag $TAG` → upload `manifest.json` artifact → `gh release upload` → `gh release edit --notes-file changelog.md --draft=false`. Publishing is the last step, so **failure ⇒ draft stays** (the fail-closed gate).
+3. **Why chained, not event-triggered:** release-please creates tags/releases with `GITHUB_TOKEN`; per GitHub's recursion prevention (and release-please's own README), those resources do **not** trigger other workflows. A chained job in the same workflow is immune to this.
+4. **Cross-plan gap flagged for PR #8:** its `release.yml` (tag push) and `e2e-install.yml` have the same suppression problem and may never fire. Remediation included in Task 4: `token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN || github.token }}` on the release-please action (PAT enables downstream triggers; also gets CI running on release PRs). Ops prerequisite documented, not code-blocking.
+5. Ordering: draft release + tag → changelog generated/validated/published → asset builds attach to the now-public release. If builds land first (race), they attach to the draft — invisible until publish; harmless.
+
+**Ops prerequisites:** repo secrets `AGENTIC_ODI_CHANGELOG_MODEL`, `AGENTIC_ODI_CHANGELOG_API_KEY`, optional `AGENTIC_ODI_CHANGELOG_BASE_URL`; optional `RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN` PAT; branch protection requiring `CI green` + `convention`; squash-merge-only merge setting (repo settings, manual).
+
+## Runtime UX
+
+### `odi changelog`
+
+```
+odi changelog                 # everything since the last version whose notes were shown
+odi changelog --since 0.1.0   # explicit lower bound (exclusive)
+odi changelog --all           # every published release with notes
+odi changelog --json          # machine-readable array of changelog.json objects
+```
+
+- **State:** `last_changelog_version` added to PR #8's `update.json` (`paths.state_file()`, under the install root). It advances **only after notes are displayed** — that is how "no gaps" and "since the version you last ran" are reconciled: the marker remembers the version whose changes the user last *saw*, so skipped versions accumulate instead of being silently marked read. Missing marker (fresh install) ⇒ show all available releases once, then set the marker. `--since` is ad-hoc and does not move the marker.
+- **Hint:** on a TTY, ordinary commands print one line when the marker exists and is behind the running version: `New in v0.2.0 — run '<prog> changelog' to see what changed.` (skipped for `changelog`/`version`/`update`, non-TTY, `--version`). After a successful `odi update`, append: `Run '<prog> changelog' to see what's new.`
+- **Fetch:** `GET /repos/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases?per_page=100` (prereleases skipped), then each release's `changelog.json` asset via its `browser_download_url`; malformed/missing assets are skipped per release. Injectable fetch callable (stdlib `urllib`, no new deps); 10s timeout; `User-Agent: agentic-odi-changelog`.
+- **Copy (exact):**
+  - header: `What's new since v0.1.0` / `All published releases`
+  - no gap: `You're up to date — no changes since v0.1.0.`
+  - nothing published: `No published releases yet.`
+  - empty release: `  (No user-facing changes.)`
+  - fetch failure: `Couldn't fetch release notes — check your connection and try again.` (exit 1, no traceback)
+  - invalid `--since`: `Invalid version: <x>` (exit 1)
+  - footer (once, at end): the disclosure constant.
+- **Rendering:** plain text, no ANSI, sections in fixed order (Initial release → Added → Improved → Fixed → Security → Removed), empty sections omitted, entries as `  • text` with `Breaking change: ` prefix when flagged.
+
+### Future GUI
+
+`core.changelog` (models, fetch, range, render) is the shared module; the Streamlit client calls it unchanged. Out of scope here beyond keeping the module GUI-ready.
+
+## Backfill Strategy (0.1.0 "Initial release")
+
+- No tags exist yet; history is 64 commits, 51 conventional, 5 merge commits, 13 non-conforming.
+- When release-please cuts `v0.1.0`, `generate.py` finds no previous `v*` tag ⇒ **initial mode** automatically: manifest = full history (`git log v0.1.0`), merge commits excluded, bodies truncated harder (subjects + files only beyond 200 commits — cheap token discipline).
+- Prompt variant: the single section is **"Initial release"** — highlights of what the product does for the user, each entry still citing real SHAs. Coverage gate applies only to parseable `feat/fix/perf/revert` commits (the legacy non-conforming minority is exempt, per the honest definition above).
+- If generation fails on first release: runbook path — regenerate locally with the same script, `gh release upload` + `gh release edit --draft=false`.
+
+## Review Focus (likely to bite)
+

+2. **GITHUB_TOKEN suppression** breaks tag/release-event triggers — chained job is safe; PR #8's `release.yml` gap flagged with PAT remediation. (Task 4)
+3. **Coverage gate false-fails on messy history**: merge commits and unparseable legacy subjects are exempt; verified against the real repo history by the local harness. (Task 3)
+4. **Grounding heuristic false positives** block releases: hard/soft split (G6a/G6b) + soft tokens only warn. (Task 3)

+6. **Range/edge behavior**: marker ≥ current, unsorted/non-semver tags, releases without assets, prereleases, `--since` invalid/out-of-range, offline mode. (Tasks 2, 5)
+7. **Offline-harness drift**: fixtures are schema-validated in CI against the same pydantic models the runtime uses. (Task 3)
+8. **Token budget** of the initial-release manifest (64 commits and growing): body/file caps. (Task 3)
+

+
+1. **Prose mechanism:** fully automated AI rewrite at release time, AI disclaimer, guardrails ensuring output is grounded in source material.
+2. **Branch naming:** Conventional Branch standard.
+3. **Distribution:** fetch from GitHub Releases — CLI (later GUI) computes all changes since the version the user last ran.

+2. **Human publish gate → fail-closed draft:** "fully automated" is honored (nothing to review per release); the safety mechanism is validation-failure ⇒ draft never publishes.
+3. **Code layout:** models/range/fetch/render live in `core/src/core/changelog.py` (shared with future GUI, stdlib fetch, injectable); generator + guardrails live in `scripts/changelog/` (release-time only, stdlib-only, no workspace deps added).

## Locked decisions
- **Standard:** Conventional Commits + Conventional Branch names + semver tags `vX.Y.Z`.
- **Prose:** fully automated AI rewrite, each release carries an AI disclaimer, with grounding guardrails.
- **Runtime delivery:** CLI/GUI fetches `changelog.json` from GitHub Releases.

## Design

**1. The standard (repo convention, enforced)**
- Commit: `type(scope): subject`. Types: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`. Scopes = packages (`cli`, `client`, `connectors`, `core`, `mcp_server`, `local_server`) plus `ci`, `deps`, `release`, `workspace`. Breaking change = `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
- Branch: `feature/`, `fix/`, `hotfix/`, `chore/`, `docs/`, `refactor/`, `test/`, `release/` + `kebab-case`.
- Semver: breaking→major, `feat`→minor, else patch (pre-1.0 breaking may be a builder call to map to minor).
- Enforcement: `commitizen` (`cz check`) as a `commit-msg` pre-commit hook + `cz commit`; CI checks the **PR title** and the **branch name**. This requires **squash-only merges** with conventional PR titles — which also cleans up going forward (your existing history is mixed: bare `Add …`, `Refactor architecture: …`, plus merge commits).

**2. The generator (release-time, AI)**
- Input = a **grounding manifest**: every commit since the last tag (sha, subject, body, PR number, files changed, diffstat). This is the only source material.
- A provider-agnostic script (`scripts/changelog/generate.py`, reusing the OpenAI SDK already in `client`) rewrites entries into user-facing prose grouped as **Added / Improved / Fixed / Removed / Security**, temperature 0, schema-constrained JSON.
- **Guardrails:** every entry must cite ≥1 source sha; any sha not in the manifest is rejected; entries with no source are rejected; a coverage check flags user-visible commits that vanished; a grounding heuristic flags proper-nouns/idents not present in source; the run fails closed. Output is a draft the maintainer approves before publish.

**3. Storage/delivery**
- A tag-triggered workflow writes the result to the GitHub Release body and uploads `changelog.json` (schema-validated) as a release asset. Each release carries the AI disclaimer (in prose and a `generated_by: "ai"` field).

**4. Runtime ("since the version you last ran")**
- `changelog.json` embeds `{version, date, sections[], sources[], generated_by}`.
- Shared pure model/render + stdlib fetch live in **`core`** (so CLI *and* the Streamlit GUI reuse them). CLI exposes `odi whats-new` / `odi changelog [--since X.Y.Z] [--all] [--json]`. The distribution plan's state file gains `last_run_version`; the command shows entries between that and the installed version, then updates state.

**5. Backfill**
- Pre-`0.1.0` messy history is summarized by the same AI process into a single grounded **"Initial release (0.1.0)"** entry.

- **Standard:** Conventional Commits + Conventional Branch names + semver tags `vX.Y.Z`.

## Design

**1. The standard (repo convention, enforced)**
- Commit: `type(scope): subject`. Types: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`. Scopes = packages (`cli`, `client`, `connectors`, `core`, `mcp_server`, `local_server`) plus `ci`, `deps`, `release`, `workspace`. Breaking change = `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
- Branch: `feature/`, `fix/`, `hotfix/`, `chore/`, `docs/`, `refactor/`, `test/`, `release/` + `kebab-case`.
- Semver: breaking→major, `feat`→minor, else patch (pre-1.0 breaking may be a builder call to map to minor).
- Enforcement: `commitizen` (`cz check`) as a `commit-msg` pre-commit hook + `cz commit`; CI checks the **PR title** and the **branch name**. This requires **squash-only merges** with conventional PR titles — which also cleans up going forward (your existing history is mixed: bare `Add …`, `Refactor architecture: …`, plus merge commits).

**2. The generator (release-time, AI)**
- Input = a **grounding manifest**: every commit since the last tag (sha, subject, body, PR number, files changed, diffstat). This is the only source material.
- A provider-agnostic script (`scripts/changelog/generate.py`, reusing the OpenAI SDK already in `client`) rewrites entries into user-facing prose grouped as **Added / Improved / Fixed / Removed / Security**, temperature 0, schema-constrained JSON.
- **Guardrails:** every entry must cite ≥1 source sha; any sha not in the manifest is rejected; entries with no source are rejected; a coverage check flags user-visible commits that vanished; a grounding heuristic flags proper-nouns/idents not present in source; the run fails closed. Output is a draft the maintainer approves before publish.

**3. Storage/delivery**
- A tag-triggered workflow writes the result to the GitHub Release body and uploads `changelog.json` (schema-validated) as a release asset. Each release carries the AI disclaimer (in prose and a `generated_by: "ai"` field).

**4. Runtime ("since the version you last ran")**
- `changelog.json` embeds `{version, date, sections[], sources[], generated_by}`.
- Shared pure model/render + stdlib fetch live in **`core`** (so CLI *and* the Streamlit GUI reuse them). CLI exposes `odi whats-new` / `odi changelog [--since X.Y.Z] [--all] [--json]`. The distribution plan's state file gains `last_run_version`; the command shows entries between that and the installed version, then updates state.

**5. Backfill**
- Pre-`0.1.0` messy history is summarized by the same AI process into a single grounded **"Initial release (0.1.0)"** entry.

# First-Run Onboarding (PM Baseline) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** On first interactive launch, the CLI captures a PM baseline via URL auto-detect with typed fallback, persists it to `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json`, and exposes `setup`/`profile` commands; the first-run hook never fires again once the file exists.

**Architecture:** Three new modules in the `cli` package: `profile.py` (baseline model, XDG config path, atomic load/save, `setup`/`profile` Typer sub-app), `infer.py` (deterministic keyword-based domain/business-model inference from page text), `onboard.py` (httpx fetch + stdlib HTML signal extraction, confirmation card, typed fallback, first-run hook). The hook is wired into the existing root Typer callback in `cli.py`.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.10+, Typer, httpx (new declared `cli` dependency), stdlib `html.parser`, pytest, uv.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-first-run-onboarding-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- Python `>= 3.10`; CLI package `agentic-odi-cli`, entry `cli.cli:app`.
- Config dir: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agentic-odi` → `~/.config/agentic-odi` (Windows: `%APPDATA%\agentic-odi`); baseline file `baseline.json`.
- All user-facing copy renders the invoked program name via `Path(sys.argv[0]).name` (helper `cli.cli_name()`), never a hard-coded `odi`/`agentic-odi`.
- No LLM calls, no network in tests (httpx `MockTransport` only), no writes outside the XDG config dir (tests override `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` / `HOME` via monkeypatch + tmp_path).
- Schema: only `schema_version` is required; all other fields may be `null`/empty; confirmation card renders only non-null lines. JSON keys are **flat** (`product_name`, `product_url`) rather than the spec's nested `product` object — simpler for the dataclass round-trip (builder call).
- `--version` needs no guard in the hook: the eager Typer option callback raises `Exit` during parsing, before the root callback body runs.

name: release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: linux_x86_64
            container: quay.io/pypa/manylinux2014_x86_64:latest
          - os: linux
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            target: linux_arm64
            container: quay.io/pypa/manylinux2014_aarch64:latest
          - os: macos
            runner: macos-14
            target: macos_arm64
          - os: macos
            runner: macos-13
            target: macos_x86_64
          - os: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            target: windows_x86_64
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    container: ${{ matrix.container }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup uv
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          uv-version: "0.8.22"
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Build
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          RELEASE_DATE_UTC: ${{ github.event.repository.pushed_at || github.event.head_commit.timestamp }}
        run: |
          VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          RELEASE_DATE_UTC=$(git log -1 --format=%cI)
          export VERSION RELEASE_DATE_UTC
          bash scripts/build_binary.sh
      - name: Generate checksums
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          for f in odi_*.tar.gz odi_*.zip; do echo "hash $f"; done
          if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            sha256sum odi_*.tar.gz odi_*.zip > checksums.txt 2>/dev/null || true
          elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            shasum -a 256 odi_*.tar.gz odi_*.zip > checksums.txt 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
        shell: bash
      - name: Upload assets
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: |
            odi_*.tar.gz
            odi_*.zip
            checksums.txt

  upload-installers:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Upload install scripts
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: |
            scripts/install.sh
            scripts/install.ps1
